correctness.rationale: For each m>=3 and t>0 the weighted Laplacian is the tensor sum of a cycle Laplacian and the 2-by-2 rung Laplacian. Reduced cycle eigenvalues are strictly increasing, with real eigenspace dimensions d_j=1 at endpoints and 2 inside. Each distinct level combines at most one subspace per parity band; hence the highest multiplicity is exactly max(2,d_j+d_k over 2t=nu_k-nu_j). Symmetric PBH gives the lower bound. The selected nested S2/S3/S4 achieve injective eigenvector restriction: Fourier evaluation at cycle offsets 0,1 has determinant sin(2*pi*j/m) unequal to zero for all interior j; a scalar-plus-double collision yields abs determinant 2*abs(sin); a double-plus-double collision separates by vertical parity into two nonsingular Fourier blocks. Scalar-plus-scalar at even m and t=2 remains rank two. The proof handles simultaneous resonances at different eigenvalues. Independently 10 exact-rational m,t tests and 550 numerical parameter tests with 9634 PBH ranks were reproduced using bundled verify.py; these finite tests are not substitutes for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The natural and widely studied circular-ladder family is a minimal model of two-layer coupled cycle networks. Exact spectral resonances can double the minimum number of independently controlled nodes from 2 to 4, with smaller scalar/double transitions at 3 and a harmless scalar/scalar collision at 2 for even circumference. The theorem reduces every size and continuous positive rung parameter to explicit finite arithmetic frequency differences, and one fixed spatially localized nested set of 2/3/4 nodes is provably optimal throughout. This is a complete natural design classification, not a small numeric table, renaming or incidental deduction.
